plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
This plan prioritizes de-risking and reducing overall portfolio volatility.
It aims to establish a large cash buffer by liquidating higher-risk assets.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating all leveraged ETFs and high-beta names. Expect lower drawdowns but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU) to reduce overall leverage.
Trim QQQI to 24% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy COP at 4% as a new, high-quality long setup from the scanner.
This plan balances growth with risk management, maintaining a small cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month growth, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a strong new setup. Expect moderate drawdowns with reasonable upside potential.

plan: Add to all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU) to increase exposure.
Trim QQQI to 24% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy COP at 6% as a new, high-quality long setup from the scanner.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for aggressive growth, with strict stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth by stretching leverage and concentration. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lead to substantial losses quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero for income focus.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
It aims to park cash for yield, reducing exposure to high-beta names.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on steady distributions and capital preservation. It significantly reduces growth potential in favor of income and lower volatility. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
